headline: South Australia has named three commissioners, led by former Federal Court judge Iain Ross, to run its Royal Commission into artificial intelligence.
score_reason: Pool 4 lowered by 1: the appointments were made on 1 Oct 2026, before the window, and ABC News (Australia)'s report of them was already in the 2 Oct pool.
importance_line: South Australians, from students and workers to users of public services, are to be asked for their views through submissions and forums on how the state handles AI, but the inquiry's final report is not due until mid 2027 and this article relays the government's own announcement.
source: Inside State Government, citing the South Australian Government
summary: Inside State Government, relaying the South Australian Government's announcement, reports that economist and former Federal Court judge Dr Iain Ross was appointed on Thursday 1 Oct 2026 to chair the state's Royal Commission (a formal public inquiry) into artificial intelligence, alongside Kate Pounder, the Tech Council of Australia's first chief executive, and Stanford University AI expert Professor Christopher Manning. The inquiry will examine AI's effects on education, jobs, regulation, community life and public services in South Australia, will take public submissions and hold community forums, and is expected to hand its final report to government in mid 2027.
notes: Read in full on Inside State Government, which relays the South Australian Government's announcement; the Government's own release was not opened. The appointments were made on 1 Oct 2026 and the Terms of Reference were published with them (date not stated). ABC News (Australia)'s report of the appointments was in the 2 Oct pool.
